meta.title: Lev IR in 60 seconds
meta.description: One page: what Leviathan's internal representation is, how a change moves through it, and why the system can build itself.

props.title: One graph, patched toward its ideal state
props.subtitle: Leviathan keeps a structured description of everything it manages. Every request becomes a patch to that description. The system compiles the description into the artifact: code, docs, a video, a plugin. That is the whole idea.
props.meta: Read time about a minute · Projection of the 2026-09-29 rulings

props.label: The shape
props.title: Three layers, six facets, seven stages, one unit of change

props.content:
**3 layers** · ontology (what can exist) · instances (what does exist) · projections (generated views)

**6 facets** · structure · work · policy · execution · knowledge · vocabulary (the last two are provisional)

**7 lifecycle stages** · ephemeral → captured → classified → crystallizing → crystallized → manifesting → completed

**1 unit of change** · the graph patch: current state → target state

props.caption: Rows are layers, columns are facets. A video landing page, a coding rule, a task and a word all have a cell.

**Ontology** is the small schema: kinds, their relations, their lifecycle stages. **Instances** are the material graph: this task, this module, this check, this flow. **Projections** are anything generated from instances and never edited by hand.

**Lev IR** is ontology plus instances. A file is IR when it is an instance of a declared kind, whether or not code reads every field. A field no kind declares is cruft, which makes hygiene a diff, not a review.

props.label: The loop
props.title: How a request becomes a change

props.caption: Shaping happens in the early stages; canonizing only after crystallization. Ambiguity goes to the human. Compilation is deterministic.

**Example.** Three properties: a SaaS app, a marketing site, a video campaign. A request arrives: host a video on a landing page and link to it from the app. That is new content in two existing kinds (page, link) and one new instance produced by the video domain module. The patch adds a video node, a page field and a link relation. Admission checks the kinds and owners. Exec compiles: a landing page build, an app link, a rendered video. No new plugin was needed.

If the request had been "we need to manage podcasts," there is no podcast kind. That is new structure: the patch proposes a kind and a module. Admission asks the human, because minting a kind is a ruling. Once ruled, the system builds the module. That is how Leviathan grows its own plugins.

rows.m: the internal representation: ontology plus instances, in stages candidate → admitted → resolved. Bare 'IR' means this.
the schema layer: kinds, relations, lifecycle stages. Base kinds in core; modules add namespaced kinds.
a folder Lev looks inside: a project, a module, a task.
a fractal root that owns folder names (`owns:`) or declares kinds.
a module's declaration of which folders it owns in every fractal root and what each file means.
the one pipeline that finds roots, collects ownership, rejects conflicts and hands each owner its files.
the compiled form of one flow; a run is one execution of it; a trigger starts it; a hook is where it attaches.
the diff from the material graph's current state to its target state, as add/modify operations.
`task.yaml` inside a task's fractal root; `exec.yaml` says how it runs.
where an idea or work item sits: ephemeral → captured → classified → crystallizing → crystallized → manifesting → completed. The ideal state is the target plus this stage.

props.content:
**Do not canonize input.** A person's words are intent, not vocabulary. Every message is mapped to an existing term and owner, or marked unmapped and asked about. Names are minted only after an idea has crystallized, and only by ruling.

**Only the deterministic engine decides.** Models propose observations and patches. Admission, checks and verdicts run in code with a test that proves they can fail. That is why the ratchet only moves forward, and why the system can be trusted to build itself.

props.label: On disk
props.title: What a patch and an ownership claim look like

props.content:
# a module declaring what it owns in every fractal root (target shape)
owns:
  video:
    code: [src/video/**]
    means: operation
  media/:
    means: media record

# a graph patch, the unit of change (shape of the existing graph.patch event)
type: graph.patch
source: operator-node
data:
  operations:
    - op: add_node
      kind: video
      id: lev://video/launch-teaser
      produced_by: plugins/video
    - op: set_field
      target: lev://page/landing
      field: hero_media
      value: lev://video/launch-teaser
    - op: add_relation
      from: lev://app/main
      to: lev://page/landing
      relation: links_to

**Words used above, one line each.** The **material graph** is the set of instances and their relations, what actually exists right now. The **ideal state** is the target value of each instance plus its lifecycle stage. **Admission** is the deterministic check that lets a patch into the graph or rejects it; it only moves forward, which is why it is called a ratchet. The two stage lists are different axes: candidate → admitted → resolved is what happens to one patch; ephemeral → completed is where an idea or work item sits in its life.
